analysis.title: Stocks Panicked, Credit Yawned: Who's Right?
key_insights: Since the midterm results the S&P 500 is down 2.8%, driven entirely by 72 S&P 500 AI infrastructure beneficiaries (semis, power, networking, cooling), which fell 13.3% in two days while the five hyperscalers gained 1.7% and the rest of the index was flat.

The AI spending beneficiaries have given up their year-to-date outperformance even though their next-12-month earnings estimates have risen more than 50% relative to the S&P 500. Their forward P/E is 13.1x, a 26% discount to the S&P 500's 17.8x, the lowest relative and absolute level since late 2022.
S&P semis trade at 13.9x forward earnings versus a historical median of 17.3x, after peaking above 30x twice in the past two years.
Catalyst was the midterm result. Goldman sees state data center moratoria potentially freezing roughly 45% of planned US capacity, with Georgia, Ohio and Michigan following Texas.

Wilson's view is that a moratorium acts like a moat: constrained supply lifts pricing for existing compute and data center capacity, lowers hyperscaler capex outlays, and gives owners of capacity a strategic advantage. The goal-post shift is that, as in 1H26 when capex recipients outperformed spenders, post-midterm trading again maps to capex flows but in reverse.
Goldman's megacap tech basket vs its broad AI basket ratio rose from about 1.21 in June to about 1.92, near its one-year high, and regained half of its three-week underperformance vs the S&P.
Friday evidence of scarcity: Microsoft cancelled capacity rented from Oracle because older Nvidia hardware no longer fit its specifications, and Alphabet then sought capacity.
Goldman's custom baskets desk (Louis Miller) likes owning the rebound in Hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR) as positioning approaches washout, via a Jan 110/120 call spread costing 1.8%.

Thursday's 4.4% S&P drop was the worst day since April 2025 (Liberation Day), but the generic 30y IG spread widened only 2.2bps versus 8.2bps expected from regression. Goldman credit strategist Reid Zhou says credit's downside convexity hasn't kicked in yet.

Wilson attributes IG's calm to the selloff hitting spending recipients, and to eased credit supply concerns as data center builds face political friction. Credit had been under pressure for months as AI spenders reached deeper into credit funding.

Hedge from Miller's desk: short generic IG 30-year basket (GSIG30AS) on swap, rates-hedged, against a beta-weighted long in S&P futures. Sized as selling $500 million of GSIG30AS against buying roughly 143 ESZ6 contracts, exploiting the currently low credit-equity beta.

Hyperscaler issuance was $67 billion in the last week across five bond deals, taking YTD issuance to $296 billion, almost $50 billion above Goldman's assumption for the calendar year. Goldman has not yet cut its 2027 estimates.

Wilson concludes the biggest issuers are likely ahead of themselves on required funding so future supply realises below current estimates. Goldman's Amanda Lynam still expects about $440 billion of direct hyperscaler issuance plus $300 billion of project finance in 2027, with near-term risks firmly tilted toward spread widening.
High yield and AI credit already reacted: data center CDS widened past 500bps Thursday (a record) and CoreWeave bond spreads topped 1,200bps.

ZeroHedge's own view (not Goldman's) sides with the credit desk, reading the 2bp IG move on a 4.4% equity fall as complacency, and notes Friday's 165K payrolls put a December rate hike back on the table.

tension_points.bull_case: Moratoria act as a moat: existing data center capacity gains pricing power, hyperscaler capex falls and credit supply eases, so hyperscalers rally (Goldman's Wilson).
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscalers have issued $296B YTD, with Goldman credit expecting about $440B direct plus $300B project finance in 2027 and near-term risks tilted toward spread widening. IG's downside convexity may not have kicked in yet.
tension_points.what_invalidates: IG spreads widening toward the regression-implied level (8.2bps for a 4.4% equity drop) or hyperscalers needing bond market funding more than the market needs them.

theme_stances.key_argument: Data center moratoria constrain supply, boosting pricing and strategic advantage for owners of existing compute while cutting capex.
theme_stances.evidence: supply discipline would both boost pricing for constrained compute & datacentre capacity

theme_stances.key_argument: IG spreads barely moved on a 4.4% equity drop while heavy hyperscaler issuance continues, so downside convexity may still arrive.
theme_stances.evidence: credit's downside convexity hasn't kicked in...yet
